def run_anova_decomposition(df, sigma_value=0.3):

The ONLY thing missing is the noise level: the parameter defaults to 0.3 and is never passed. WHAT TO CHANGE: (1) add a module constant beside PRIMARY_STRATEGY at :76, `PERFORMANCE_ANOVA_SIGMAS = [0.0, 0.3, 0.6]` — 0.0 gives clean R2, 0.6 is the author's reporting level, 0.3 is retained so the existing published number stays reproducible; (2) at :2796-2804 change `perf_results[strategy] = perf` to key on `(strategy, sigma)` and loop the new constant inside the strategy loop; (3) return `sigma` in the dict at :1994-2001; (4) the table rows built at :2872-2885 gain a `Sigma` column and become one row per (Strategy, Sigma). At sigma=0.6 more cells are sparse, so the two sigma levels would silently run on different model rosters and the eta-squared shares would not be comparable — which is precisely the comparison being asked for. Use the MIN_CELL_ITERS rule here too and print the roster for every sigma. Also record the undeclared filter at :1946 (`df_sigma['r2'] > -10`) as a counted column rather than a silent drop. items.headline: Spec 2 — rebuild the paired significance tests per noise type on all three quantities; the current test ignores both arguments meant to hold a condition fixed.
items.verbatim:
def wilcoxon_paired_test(auc_df, model_base, model_variant, rep=None, strategy='legacy'):
    """
    Wilcoxon signed-rank test for paired model comparison.

    Pairs models across all shared (rep, strategy) conditions to get enough
    matched observations. Falls back to single rep×strategy if pairing across
    conditions yields too few points.
    """
    if rep is None:
        rep = PRIMARY_REP
    # Pair across all shared conditions (rep × strategy) for sufficient n
    base_data = auc_df[auc_df['model'] == model_base]
    var_data = auc_df[auc_df['model'] == model_variant]

The pairing key at :1909-1910 is `.set_index(['rep', 'strategy'])`, so every test pools all reps and all strategies. items.why_it_matters: WHAT EXISTS ALREADY: a Wilcoxon function, and a table3_wilcoxon_tests.csv writer at :3357-3359 covering five model pairs. Nothing else — one quantity only (auc_norm), and pooled across everything. WHAT TO CHANGE: (1) new signature `wilcoxon_paired_test(metric_df, model_base, model_variant, metric_col, rep, strategy)`; filter to that rep and that strategy at the top; pair on the replicate column ('iteration' on QM9, 'fold' on validation) instead of on (rep, strategy). This requires the per-replicate metric frame in spec 5 note A — the current auc_df has one row per cell and cannot supply pairs. (2) At the call site :3317-3351, loop the six strategies from STRATEGY_ORDER and the three quantities. (3) DELETE the misleading docstring sentence about a fallback. THE CONSEQUENCE THE AUTHOR MUST SEE BEFORE THIS SHIPS: pairing within one strategy at one rep gives n = 10 (QM9 replicates) or n = 5 (validation folds), not 36. At n = 5 the two-sided signed-rank test has a minimum attainable p of 0.0625 and can NEVER reach 0.05; at n = 10 the minimum is 0.002. So the QM9 tests survive de-pooling and the validation ones do not. Report the exact p and the paired difference, and drop the significance star on validation rather than printing a test that cannot fire. (4) 5 comparisons x 6 strategies x 3 quantities = 90 tests; add a Holm-adjusted p within each quantity. OUTPUT COLUMNS: Family, Comparison, Strategy, Rep, Quantity (r2_clean | r2_at_0.6 | auc_norm), n_pairs, base_mean, variant_mean, delta, statistic, p_value, p_holm, significant. RE-RUN OR NOW: the validation half is buildable AND runnable now (5 folds present in the clean data); the QM9 half is buildable now but needs the re-run for valid numbers.

items.why_it_matters: WHAT EXISTS ALREADY: the whole decomposition is built and correct — _two_way_eta2_unbalanced (:1394-1438) uses Type-I sequential sums of squares from nested OLS fits specifically so the residual is pure within-cell variance and cannot go negative. It is not broken. It is being fed one observation per cell, so the saturated fit at :1429 reproduces the data exactly and the residual is arithmetically zero. THE FIX, in firing order: (1) at :1150 add 'fold' to dedup_cols, guarded by presence — this is the line that destroys 4 of every 5 rows; (2) in calculate_validation_auc, add 'fold' to group_cols at :1364-1366 and DELETE the `groupby('sigma')['r2'].mean()` at :1372 (with folds in the key there is nothing left to average); return one row per (dataset, model, rep, strategy, fold) carrying auc_norm, baseline_r2 (which IS clean R2) and a new r2_at_0.6; (3) the call at :1605 then sees 5 observations per cell and the residual becomes real; (4) the filter to legacy at :1596-1597 stays as the headline but loop all six noise types and emit per-strategy rows, so the show-all-six rule holds.
